insights.headline: Gold slides toward $4,130 ahead of Fed minutes; RBI rules out cuts as rupee nears record low
insights.summary: Spot gold fell about 0.8% to $4,130 an ounce as a firmer dollar and record-high long-end US yields weighed ahead of the Fed's September meeting minutes due later today. The RBI's hawkish turn deepened: the governor ruled out near-term rate cuts while economists pencilled in at least 50 bps more hikes, and the rupee slid to 96.8450, near its all-time low. China's central bank posted its biggest monthly gold reserve addition in three years, while LBMA delegates forecast $5,013 gold within a year.
points: Spot gold fell 0.8% to $4,130.37 as the dollar firmed; Fed September minutes due today with 88% odds of a December US hike priced.
RBI governor ruled out near-term cuts -- only hikes or pause ahead; economists see 50 bps more, terminal rate near 6% by March 2027.
Rupee hit 96.8450 intraday, near the 96.96 record low, ending 0.4% down at 96.7750 despite the RBI's 25 bps hike.
US 30-year yield hit a 24-year high; China's central bank made its biggest monthly gold purchase in three years.
LBMA delegates forecast gold at $5,013 and silver at $97 within 12 months; gold-silver ratio at 68 leaves gold looking pricey.

trending.title: Fed minutes loom as gold slides; MCX tracks the move
trending.summary: Gold's slide to about $4,130 reflects markets bracing for the Fed's September minutes, with record long-end yields and a firm dollar doing the damage. MCX bullion is tracking the global move lower.

trending.title: RBI's hawkish pivot: no cuts on the table
trending.summary: The RBI followed its first hike in nearly four years by ruling out cuts and signalling more tightening, seen as at least 50 bps more. The rupee is nonetheless flirting with record lows.

trending.title: Central banks keep stacking as LBMA sees $5,013 gold
trending.summary: China posted its biggest monthly reserve addition in three years, and LBMA delegates forecast $5,013 gold and $97 silver within a year -- structural demand persists beneath the rate-driven selloff.

trending.title: Diwali demand in wait-and-watch mode
trending.summary: With gold 26% off its January record, jewellers report cautious buyers ahead of Diwali; a gold-silver ratio of 68 leaves gold looking expensive relative to silver.

items.title: Gold edges lower with focus on Fed minutes, rate path clues
items.summary: Spot gold fell 0.8% to $4,130.37 an ounce as the dollar index rose 0.3%, with investors awaiting the Fed's September meeting minutes for clues on whether policymakers still lean toward further hikes. Analysts see a mild downside bias into the release, with traders pricing an 88% chance of a December hike.

items.title: RBI signals more rate hikes ahead: Could 7.25% yield level become a near-term market reference point?
items.summary: After the RBI's 25 bps hike to 5.50% and the shift to 'calibrated tightening', economists see at least 50 bps of further hikes with the terminal rate near 6% by March 2027; the governor ruled out near-term cuts, saying only hikes or a pause lie ahead. The 10-year G-sec yield hardened to about 7.25%, which traders now watch as the near-term reference level.

items.title: RBI Repo Rate Hike: Will Gold Prices Fall After Rates Rise To 5.50%? What Investors Should Know
items.summary: The RBI raised the repo rate 25 bps to 5.50% on October 7, shifting its stance to 'calibrated tightening' as inflation runs above the 4% target. Experts quoted in the piece say the hike doesn't automatically weaken gold: US interest rates, real yields, the dollar and the rupee matter more for bullion prices.

items.title: Rupee nears record low despite RBI hike, governor says markets can be irrational
items.summary: The rupee sank to an intraday low of 96.8450 per dollar, close to its 96.96 record low from May 20, and ended 0.4% lower at 96.7750 even after the RBI's 25 bps hike to 5.50%. Governor Sanjay Malhotra called short-term market behaviour 'irrational', while ANZ expects two more 25 bps hikes by March 2027.

items.title: Gold, silver prices: What is driving MCX rates on October 7
items.summary: MCX gold and silver tracked the global slide as a firmer dollar and elevated bond yields weighed on bullion ahead of the Fed's September meeting minutes. Domestic traders also weighed the RBI's hawkish policy turn and a weaker rupee, which cushions the fall in rupee terms for Indian buyers.

items.title: US 30-year bond yield hits fresh 24-year high
items.summary: The US 30-year Treasury yield climbed to its highest since 2002 as investors priced in a prolonged higher-rate regime, with the 10-year yield also edging up. Higher long-end yields lift real yields and the dollar, keeping pressure on non-yielding gold.

items.title: Gold to hit $5,000, silver $97 in the next 12 months - LBMA delegate survey
items.summary: Delegates at the 2026 LBMA Global Precious Metals Conference expect gold near $5,013 an ounce a year from now, about 20% above current spot, and silver near $94.70, Kitco reports; a UBS survey found 65% of reserve managers cite diversification as the main reason for holding gold.

items.title: China posts biggest monthly gold reserve increase in 3 years
items.summary: The People's Bank of China added 740,000 ounces of gold in September, lifting reserves to 77.47 million ounces — the largest monthly increase since September 2023 and the 23rd consecutive month of buying. China's foreign-exchange reserves dipped $38.1 billion to $3.4 trillion over the same month.

items.title: Gold caught between central bank demand and real-yield pressure: Kotak Securities
items.summary: Kotak Securities says gold is being pulled in two directions: steady central-bank buying is supporting prices while elevated real yields cap gains. The framework helps explain why bullion has struggled to rally despite persistent official-sector demand.

items.title: Silver's Supply Deficit Is Getting Harder to Fix as Copper Ore Tightens
items.summary: An Investing.com analysis argues silver's supply deficit is becoming harder to close as tightening copper ore supply constrains new output, with most silver mined as a by-product of copper and other base metals. The piece says the structural shortfall continues to underpin silver even as prices consolidate.

items.title: Gold-silver ratio at 68: Gold looks expensive, but should investors stay invested?
items.summary: The gold-silver ratio has risen to about 68:1, leaving gold looking expensive relative to silver, Moneycontrol reports; analysts quoted in the piece suggest long-term investors keep gold as the core holding and consider adding silver if the ratio starts declining with improving silver demand.

items.title: MMTC, STC may lose gold import tax advantage as GST Council weighs 3% GST
items.summary: The GST Council is likely to discuss on October 8 bringing government trading entities like MMTC and STC under the 3% GST net for precious-metal imports, ending a tax advantage held since 2017 and putting banks, nominated agencies and bullion exchanges on the same footing, the Times of India reports.

items.title: Gold corrects 26% from January record high | Is this a buying opportunity ahead of Diwali?
items.summary: Gold has corrected more than 26% from its January peak of $5,595 an ounce to around $4,100, one of its sharpest drawdowns in years, with MCX gold back below ₹1.50 lakh per 10 grams. Kotak Securities' Kaynat Chainwala traces the slide to firm inflation prints pushing Fed hike bets near 90%, while Tata Mutual Fund says central-bank buying and geopolitical uncertainty keep structural drivers intact.

items.title: Gold price dips, but buyers remain cautious ahead of Diwali
items.summary: Gold has fallen roughly Rs 8,000 per 10 grams over the past month to about Rs 1.47 lakh (excluding GST), yet buyers in Pune remain cautious ahead of Diwali. Shoppers are choosing lighter jewellery and smaller token purchases, while jewellers report steady festive-season footfall.
